sentences.text:
(At Present Lodged In Central Jail, Bikaner)
 ----Appellant  Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, Through Pp 2. Manju Devi W/o Biram Dev, B/c Meghwal, R/o Ward No.
 2, Kolayat , District Bikaner.
For Respondent(s) : Ms. Anita Gehlot, PP  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE KULDEEP MATHUR Order 20/01/2023

The instant appeal has been filed under Section 14(A) of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act on behalf of the appellant, who is in custody in connection with FIR No.124/2022 registered at Police Station Kolayat, District Bikaner, for the offences under Sections 376(1) , 504,
506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v), 3(2) (va) of SC/ST Act.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and Public Prosecutor for the State.
Perused the material available on record.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the FIR was lodged after an unexplained delay of 7-8 months from the date of incident.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that no alleged videos or photographs have been recovered in the investigation.
He further submits that the appellant is in judicial (2 of 2) [CRLAS-1736/2022] custody since long and the trial of the case will take sufficiently long time to conclude.
Thus, learned counsel submits that benefit of bail may be extended to the appellant.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel appearing for the complainant vehemently opposed the bail application.

sentences.text: Having regard to the totality of facts and circumstances as available on record and upon consideration of the arguments advanced without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court deems it proper to enlarge the appellant on bail.
Consequently, the instant appeal is allowed.
The impugned order dated 20.10.2022 passed by the Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Bikaner is set aside.

entities.text: Special Judge, SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act Cases, Bikaner
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is ordered that the accused-appellant Jitendra Singh Aka Jitu S/o Ganga Singh arrested in connection with aforesaid FIR, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided him furnish a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/- and two sureties of Rs.50,000/- each to the satisfaction of the learned lower Court with the stipulation to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 147-KshamaD/-
